clue.text: Battle to get a gang leader on trial

indicators.note: the leader of the gang is its opening letter

parts.note: someone on trial is in court, facing the judge

explanation.surface: A gang boss is put on trial.
explanation.walkthrough: AGINCOURT was the 1415 battle in which Henry V's English army defeated the French.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic English victory over France, a famous example of a battle.

clue.text: Lincoln set about American corrupt practice

indicators.note: the president's short name is placed around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: Abraham Lincoln is often called Abe

explanation.surface: President Lincoln tackles a corrupt American practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Misuse of power or a system for wrong ends is a corrupt practice.

clue.text: Child recently born to a Spanish princess

parts.note: a newborn child is an infant

explanation.surface: A Spanish princess has just given birth.
explanation.walkthrough: An INFANTA is a daughter of the Spanish or Portuguese monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal title for a daughter of the king of Spain who is not heir.

clue.text: Film gangster loses point, being cautious

indicators.note: the gangster's name drops one letter, a compass point

parts.note: James Cagney played many gangsters in Hollywood films
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A movie hoodlum stays guarded and careful.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unwilling to give information away is guarded, wary and secretive.

clue.text: Lie in furrow with hunt milling around

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the other piece, enclosing it
a crowd milling moves about in confusion, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: a rut is a groove or furrow in the ground

explanation.surface: Someone lies in a field furrow while the hunt mills about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie in' tempts as a phrase, but 'Lie' alone is the definition; 'milling' scrambles the hunt and 'around' wraps it round the furrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsehood is a lie, the opposite of the truth.

clue.text: Addressing some criticism

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both speaking directly to someone and a stern reprimand.

clue.text: Live with a university boyfriend

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: Moving in with a fellow student boyfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for a male admirer or sweetheart.

clue.text: The publican's profit is cheap at the price

parts.note: a publican's place of work is the bar
a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: A landlord's takings are good value.
explanation.walkthrough: A publican is a pub landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worth more than its cost is a good buy, a snip, cheap at the price.

clue.text: Mass trial arranged for scaremongers

indicators.note: letters arranged are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A big trial is staged for those spreading panic.
explanation.definitionFit: People who needlessly spread fear are scaremongers, raising false alarms.

clue.text: Hairstyle set before engagement party

indicators.note: the hairstyle is placed ahead of the engagement in the answer

parts.note: a bun is hair coiled at the back of the head
a military engagement is a fight

explanation.surface: Getting one's hair done before an engagement party.
explanation.walkthrough: A BUNFIGHT is British slang for a tea party or a noisy gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Humorous British term for a tea party or rowdy social function.

clue.text: Officer with a song in his heart — something catchy

indicators.note: the song goes into the middle of the officer's abbreviation

parts.note: Lt is short for lieutenant, an officer
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: An officer with a song in his heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a rope used to catch animals, so it is a catching device.

clue.text: Eagerly Len rummaged about in the locker

indicators.note: the jumbled name is placed inside the locking device

parts.note: a key is something that locks

indicators.note: rummaging stirs things around, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Len searches keenly through his locker.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with keenness and enthusiasm is doing it eagerly.

clue.text: Well informed about weapons, prepared to protest strongly

parts.note: to be up in a subject is to know it well
arms are weapons

explanation.surface: An expert on weaponry is ready to protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for being indignant and ready to fight or object vigorously.

clue.text: Fruit constantly consumed by father

indicators.note: the second piece is swallowed inside the first

parts.note: papa is a word for father
ay or aye is an old word for always

explanation.surface: Dad keeps eating fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical fruit with orange flesh, also called pawpaw.

clue.text: It's in the middle when on the level

definitions.text: It's in the middle when on the level

parts.words: It's in the middle when on the level
parts.note: a spirit level shows a surface is flat when its bubble sits centrally in the tube

explanation.walkthrough: 'on the level' sounds like honesty but means a horizontal surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The trapped pocket of gas in a spirit level centres when level.

clue.text: Current left off, having been discharged

parts.note: AC is alternating current
to have quitted is to have stopped or left off

explanation.surface: The electricity was switched off after discharge.
explanation.definitionFit: A defendant cleared and released by a court has been discharged.

clue.text: Elevation above the peerage?

definitions.meaning: a royal title ranking above dukes and earls

explanation.definitionFit: Means both loftiness and the form of address for a royal, outranking peers.

clue.text: Sailor returns in a huff, needing permission to enter port

indicators.note: the turned sailor goes inside the word for a huff

parts.note: a fit of pique is a huff

indicators.note: the sailor word is read backwards

parts.note: tar is a slang word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor comes back sulking, wanting leave to dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses the sailor and 'in' places him inside the huff; pratique is a maritime term solvers may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Pratique is the licence given to a ship to use a port after quarantine clearance.

clue.text: Become weak, get nurse round for the final stage

indicators.note: the nursing word goes round the weakness word

parts.note: to tend is to nurse
to ail is to grow sickly

explanation.surface: Falling ill and having a nurse visit near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The last part of something is its rear or final section.

clue.text: Honour Ben and Noel with new order

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order, rearranged

explanation.surface: Ben and Noel are honoured in a new order of merit.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise someone to the peerage, or to dignify, is to honour them.

clue.text: Giving an alternative sort of threat

definitions.meaning: offering another option, as in 'this or that'

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase offers another option or ends a menacing warning.

clue.text: Ban involving English doctor on Greek ship

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A ban affects an English doctor aboard a Greek vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An official prohibition on trade or shipping is a ban.

clue.text: Sound proof of what a performer can do

definitions.text: Sound proof of what a performer can do

parts.words: Sound proof of what a performer can do
parts.note: a trial hearing where an actor or singer shows their skills

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound proof' looks like soundproof, but means a test that is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial performance heard by those casting a show tests a performer's ability.

clue.text: New bride's bits and pieces

indicators.note: new means made over, so the letters take a fresh form

explanation.surface: A newlywed's odds and ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Scattered fragments and rubble are bits and pieces.

clue.text: Material that's dug up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: mined means dug

explanation.surface: Fabric that has been excavated.
explanation.definitionFit: A sturdy cotton twill used for jeans, a type of fabric.

clue.text: Putin ordered data insertion

indicators.note: the letters are ordered afresh, put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The Russian leader ordered data inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Information fed into a computer is entered data.

clue.text: Goal protest

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means an aim; as a verb, to oppose or complain.

clue.text: He suffers from a lack of balance

definitions.text: He suffers from a lack of balance

parts.words: He suffers from a lack of balance
parts.note: not unsteadiness but having no money left in a bank account

explanation.walkthrough: 'balance' suggests poise but means a bank balance.
explanation.definitionFit: A person declared insolvent cannot pay debts, having no funds.

clue.text: Quarrel that can be relatively bitter

definitions.text: Quarrel that can be relatively bitter

parts.words: Quarrel that can be relatively bitter
parts.note: 'relatively' points to relatives: long-running bitter disputes between families

explanation.definitionFit: A prolonged hostility, often between families or clans.

clue.text: Very attractive person possibly met abroad

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A gorgeous person one might meet overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for a very handsome or desirable person.
